In this lecture we are going to learn about binary search.
Now binary search is faster than the linear search because here instead of eliminating the elements
one by one, we can eliminate half of the elements of the remaining elements at any given point.
However, we have a big restriction over here, which is binary search only works with sorted arrays,
so the array has to be sorted from the lowest element to the highest, or from highest to the lowest.
To be able to use the binary search.
So let's say we have an array like this.
So to be able to use the binary search we have to first sort this array like this.
So after sorting this let's say we are looking for the element of six.
Now in case of linear search we have to start from the zeroth index and check all elements one by one
until we reach the value of six over here.
But in case of binary search, the first thing that we will do we are going to calculate the the index
of middle element.
So in this case the first index is zero and the last index is seven.
So we are going to sum up of them and divide them by two.
It's going to give us 3.5, and we are going to take the floor of this value, which means that the
index that we are looking for is three.
So then after finding the middle index, we are going to take the value of middle index and compare
it the value that we are looking for.
So in this case we are looking for six.
So if we compare six with four we see that six is greater than four.
So this means that the element that we are looking for is located at the right side of this middle index.
So this means that the elements that is located on the left, including itself, can be eliminated.
So we can eliminate these elements in this step.
Then we can do the same operation for the right side of this array.
The first element in the right side is five, which is located at the index of four, and the last element
is eight, which is located at the index of seven.
So if we calculate the middle index it's going to be 5.5.
So this means that in this case it's going to be five because we are taking the floor index.
Now if we compare the value that we are looking for with the value that is located at the index of five,

So in this case the element is located at index of five.
So we are just going to return the index of that element.
So in this case it is five.
So this is the logic behind the binary search.
